- Overweight recent sentiment spikes in forecast calibration; if sentiment rises sharply, reduce forecast overshoot.
- When sentiment is low or trending negative, model should underweight recent highs and favor mean reversion toward prior 10-15 day average.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment peaks; lagged sentiment (e.g., 3-5 day moving average) better predicts price correction than immediate sentiment.
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by true price drop, reduce subsequent forecast peaks by 5-10% to account for momentum decay.
- For 30-day horizon, model should not overestimate early-week price movement; true outcomes often show stronger downward correction in mid-to-late period.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., <0.27 for 3+ days), apply downward bias correction to forecast mean by 2-5%.
- Forecast should adjust downward if sentiment history shows increasing negative sentiment over last 5 days, even if current sentiment is neutral.
